title: Beylik of Hamid
capsule: The Beylik of Hamid was one of the Anatolian Turkish principalities (beyliks) that emerged after the fragmentation of the Sultanate of Rum following the Mongol victory at Köse Dağ (1243). Centered on Eğirdir and the lake district of southwestern Anatolia (modern Isparta province), the Hamidids took their name from their founder Dündar Bey. The dynasty sold the districts of Akşehir and Beyşehir to the Ottoman sultan Murad I around 1381, and the remaining Hamidid lands were absorbed by the Ottomans in 1391, though the dataset's attestation to 1344 reflects the period of independent rule under Dündar Bey and his immediate successors before Ottoman pressure became decisive.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The beylik's approximate territory is known from Ottoman cadastral surveys and medieval Arabic-Persian geographical sources, but precise boundaries within the Anatolian lake district are not well mapped for this period.
